title: CORNER Pricing Page Design Brief
summary: Full design brief for the Corner pricing page. Competitive analysis (Vercel, Linear, Notion), 4-tier pricing model, feature comparison matrix, FAQ, conversion optimization, responsive design, visual direction. Bobby builds, Steffen designs.
content:
CORNER Pricing Page Design Brief

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Date: 2026-03-16 For: Steffen (visual design) + Bobby (implementation) URL: corner.app/pricing Purpose: Convert visitors into trial signups. This page makes people pay.

Competitive Analysis

Studied three best-in-class SaaS pricing pages before writing this brief.

Vercel (vercel.com/pricing)

  • What works: Feature-grouped comparison model with 9 categories. Granular differentiation (not just "checkmark / no checkmark" but specific quantities: "Up to 3" vs "Up to 40" vs "Up to 1,000"). FAQ at the bottom. Clean visual hierarchy.
  • What Corner should steal: Feature grouping by category. Specific quantity limits instead of vague checkmarks. "Free forever" language for the free tier.
  • What Corner should avoid: Too many SKUs (30+). Non-technical buyers get overwhelmed. Corner's audience is plumbers and CPAs, not developers.

Linear (linear.app/pricing)

  • What works: 4 tiers with clear progression. Horizontal plan cards with a comprehensive comparison table below. Social proof (customer logos). Tooltips on features that need explanation. Color-coded checkmarks.
  • What Corner should steal: The tooltip pattern (hoverable feature explanations without cluttering the page). Color-coded status indicators. Social proof section between pricing cards and comparison table.
  • What Corner should avoid: Per-user pricing confuses non-tech buyers. Corner charges per-plan, not per-seat (until C7 multi-user).

Notion (notion.com/pricing)

  • What works: 4-tier card layout with monthly/yearly toggle. "Recommended" badge on the aspirational tier. Bulleted feature lists per card (quick scan). Categorical feature comparison below cards. Customer testimonial with video link. Clear CTA differentiation per tier.
  • What Corner should steal: Monthly/yearly toggle with savings callout. "Recommended" badge on the Growth tier. Testimonial section. Categorical comparison tables (not one massive table).
  • What Corner should avoid: The "add-on" pricing model adds complexity. Corner keeps it simple: pick a plan, everything's included at that level.

What Makes Corner Different

None of these products are selling what Corner is selling. Vercel sells infrastructure. Linear sells project management. Notion sells workspace. Corner sells an AI team that works for you while you sleep.

The pricing page needs to feel like hiring, not shopping. "Here's the team you're about to meet" energy. Not "here are features and checkmarks."

Page Structure (Top to Bottom)

Section 1: Hero

Headline: "Your AI team. Pick your plan."

Subheadline: "Every plan includes a fully private AI office, real agents that work for you, and a dashboard you'll actually enjoy using. Start free for 7 days."

Visual: Subtle isometric office illustration in the background (the Corner game view, simplified, decorative). Not interactive. Just atmosphere.

Toggle: Monthly / Yearly billing switch. Yearly shows "Save 20%" badge. Default: Monthly (transparency, lower perceived commitment).

Section 2: Plan Cards

Section 3: Social Proof Bar

Section 4: Feature Comparison Table

Section 5: FAQ

Accordion-style. 8-10 questions. Addresses the objections a prospect has at this point in the funnel.

Q: What happens during the 7-day free trial? A: You get the full plan experience. All agents, all features at your tier level. No restrictions. Your credit card is on file but won't be charged until day 8. Cancel anytime during the trial and you won't be charged a penny.

Q: Can I switch plans later? A: Yes, any time. Upgrade or downgrade from your Settings page. Upgrades take effect immediately (prorated). Downgrades take effect at the next billing cycle.

Q: What happens to my data if I cancel? A: Your workspace is archived for 90 days. You can export all your data (context files, agent outputs, decision logs) at any time. After 90 days, archived data is permanently deleted.

Q: Do I need to provide my own AI subscription? A: Yes. Corner uses Claude Code as the AI engine. You'll need an active Anthropic API key or Claude Code subscription. This keeps your AI costs transparent and under your control. We never mark up the AI cost.

Q: How is this different from ChatGPT or other AI tools? A: ChatGPT is one conversation at a time. Corner is an entire team of specialized AI agents working in parallel, with a visual dashboard that shows you what they're doing. It's the difference between texting one person and managing a whole office.

Q: What are "agents"? A: Agents are specialized AI team members. An Operations agent manages your priorities. A Calendar agent handles scheduling. An Email agent triages your inbox. Each agent has its own personality, memory, and workspace. They hand work off to each other just like real employees.

Q: Is my data private? A: Completely. Each client gets their own isolated environment. Your data is encrypted at rest and in transit. Your agents can't access any other client's data. We never use your data for training. You can export or delete everything at any time.

Q: Can I add more agents later? A: Upgrading your plan increases your agent slots. Starter has 3, Growth has 6, Scale has 10. You choose which agent types to activate. Adding an agent is instant.

Q: What kind of support do I get? A: All plans include email support. Growth adds live chat. Scale includes monthly strategy calls with the AOM team to optimize your AI operations. Enterprise gets a dedicated account manager and quarterly business reviews.

Q: Do you offer annual billing? A: Yes. Annual billing saves you 20% compared to monthly. You can switch to annual billing at any time from your Settings page.

Section 6: Bottom CTA

Full-width section. Final conversion push.

Headline: "See it for yourself."

Subheadline: "Your AI team is 2 minutes away. Free for 7 days. No setup required."

CTA: "Start Your Free Trial" (large, centered, primary button)

Secondary: "Or contact us for a demo" (text link below button)

Visual Design Direction (For Steffen)

Overall Feel

The pricing page should feel like the rest of the Corner site: clean, spacious, white. "Heaven" aesthetic. But with enough structure to make comparison easy. The page has two jobs: (1) make the quick buyer click "Start Free Trial" within 10 seconds, and (2) give the careful buyer every detail they need without leaving the page.

Plan Card Design

  • White cards with subtle border (1px, #E5E5E5) and shadow (sm)
  • Growth card has a highlighted border (brand color) and "Recommended" badge
  • Enterprise card has a slightly different background (very light gray or subtle gradient) to differentiate from the other 3
  • Price is the largest text on each card (32-40px). Plan name above it (18-20px). Description below (14-16px).
  • CTA button fills the card width. Growth card button is the most prominent (brand color background). Other cards have secondary button styling.

Feature Comparison Table

  • Clean table. Alternating row backgrounds (white / #FAFAFA)
  • Category headers: bold, slightly larger, with a subtle left border accent
  • Checkmarks: filled circle with check for included, empty circle for excluded. Not just text "Yes" / "-"
  • Text values (quantities like "3", "6", "10") centered in cells
  • Sticky header row (plan names) on scroll
  • On mobile: comparison table becomes horizontally scrollable with sticky left column (feature names). Or: select a plan, see that plan's features in a vertical list (Linear's approach).
  • Tooltips: hover over feature name shows a 1-2 sentence explanation. Use the title attribute or a custom tooltip component with a small "?" icon.

Typography

  • Headings: Inter or system font, weight 600-700
  • Body: Inter or system font, weight 400
  • Price numbers: larger weight (700), potentially different font for emphasis
  • Feature list: 14-16px, regular weight, plenty of line height (1.6)

Spacing

  • Generous. Don't cram. The page should breathe.
  • Section padding: 80-120px vertical between major sections
  • Card padding: 32-40px internal
  • Card gap: 24px between cards on desktop

Colors

  • Primary CTA: brand color (whatever Steffen's current brand guidelines specify)
  • Growth card highlight: brand color border
  • Text: #111 (headings), #333 (body), #666 (secondary/descriptions)
  • Checkmarks: brand color for included, #CCC for excluded
  • Background: white (#FFFFFF), table alternating rows (#FAFAFA)
  • FAQ section: very light background (#F8F8F8) to visually separate from table

Responsive Behavior

Breakpoint Layout
Desktop (1024px+) 4 cards side by side. Full comparison table.
Tablet (768-1023px) 2x2 card grid. Comparison table scrollable horizontally.
Mobile (390-767px) Cards stacked vertically. Comparison: plan selector dropdown + vertical feature list (one plan at a time). Or horizontal scroll.

Interactions

  • Monthly/Yearly toggle: smooth price animation (numbers count up/down). "Save 20%" badge appears/disappears.
  • Plan card hover: subtle lift (translateY -2px, shadow increase). Not dramatic.
  • CTA button hover: darken/lighten. Standard button hover.
  • FAQ accordion: smooth expand/collapse with rotate arrow icon.
  • Comparison table tooltips: appear on hover/tap with 200ms delay.
  • Scroll behavior: smooth scroll to comparison table when "Compare plans" link is clicked.

Bobby's Implementation Checklist

Page Structure

  • Hero section (headline, subheadline, billing toggle)
  • Billing toggle component (monthly/yearly, localStorage remembers preference)
  • 4 plan cards (responsive grid)
  • "Recommended" badge on Growth card
  • Plan card CTA buttons (route to signup with plan pre-selected)
  • Social proof bar (logos or testimonial)
  • Feature comparison table (9 categories)
  • Sticky plan header row on scroll
  • Tooltips on feature names
  • FAQ accordion (8-10 items)
  • Bottom CTA section
  • Responsive: desktop, tablet, mobile layouts

Pricing Logic

  • Prices stored in a config file (not hardcoded in JSX). Easy to update.
  • Monthly/yearly price calculation (yearly = monthly * 0.8 * 12, displayed as monthly equivalent)
  • Price animation on toggle switch (countUp library or CSS transition)
  • "Save 20%" badge appears only when yearly is NOT selected (incentive to switch)

Routing

  • URL: /pricing (public, no auth required)
  • CTA "Start Free Trial" routes to /signup?plan=starter (or growth, scale)
  • CTA "Contact Sales" routes to /book (existing booking page)
  • "Compare plans" anchor link scrolls to comparison table

SEO

  • Page title: "Pricing | Corner - AI Operations Platform"
  • Meta description: "Choose your plan. 3 AI agents starting at $1,500/month. 7-day free trial, no restrictions. See what your AI team can do."
  • Open Graph image (Steffen designs a 1200x630 pricing summary card)
  • Structured data: Product schema with pricing offers

Accessibility

  • All plan cards keyboard-navigable
  • FAQ accordion keyboard-accessible (Enter to expand, Escape to collapse)
  • Comparison table screen-reader friendly (proper th/td, scope attributes)
  • Tooltips accessible via keyboard (focus, not just hover)
  • Billing toggle has aria-label: "Switch between monthly and yearly billing"
  • Color contrast AA compliant on all text

Performance

  • No heavy images (isometric background is CSS/SVG, not a large PNG)
  • Page loads in <2s on 3G
  • No JavaScript required to see prices (SSR the pricing data)
  • Comparison table lazy-loaded below the fold (intersection observer)

Steffen's Design Deliverables

  1. Pricing card design (4 variations: standard, highlighted/recommended, enterprise, hover state)
  2. Feature comparison table styling (category headers, checkmark icons, tooltip design)
  3. Billing toggle component (monthly/yearly switch with animation spec)
  4. Social proof bar layout (logo placement, testimonial card)
  5. FAQ accordion styling (expand/collapse, arrow icon, section background)
  6. Bottom CTA section (full-width, final push)
  7. Mobile layout wireframes (cards stacked, comparison adapted)
  8. OG image (1200x630 pricing summary for social sharing)
  9. Responsive breakpoint behaviors (how each section adapts)

Pricing Rationale (For Internal Reference)

Why These Numbers

Tier Monthly Yearly (per month) Margin Analysis
Starter $1,500 $1,200 CC subscription ~$100/mo + infra ~$25/mo = $125 cost. $1,375 margin (92%).
Growth $3,000 $2,400 CC subscription ~$100/mo + infra ~$25/mo + furniture CDN ~$10/mo = $135 cost. $2,865 margin (95%).
Scale $5,000 $4,000 CC subscription ~$200/mo (more agents = more API usage) + infra ~$40/mo + support time ~$200/mo = $440 cost. $4,560 margin (91%).
Enterprise $10,000+ Custom Dedicated infra ~$200/mo + CC ~$400/mo + support ~$500/mo = $1,100 cost. $8,900+ margin (89%+).

These margins are sustainable. Infrastructure costs are extremely low because CC does the heavy lifting via API calls, not local compute. The real cost is AOM's time (support calls, strategy sessions), which is accounted for in Scale and Enterprise tiers.

Why 3 Public Tiers + Enterprise

  • Starter catches the cautious buyer. "I want to try AI but I'm not ready to commit big." Low enough that it's approachable. High enough that it filters out non-serious leads.
  • Growth is the target tier. Most buyers should land here. "Recommended" badge + the full feature set makes it the obvious choice. The price gap between Starter ($1,500) and Growth ($3,000) makes Growth feel like a deal (2x the agents, all modes, all features for 2x the price).
  • Scale is for power users and the aspiration anchor. It makes Growth feel reasonable by comparison. A $3k/month plan seems like a bargain when $5k is right next to it.
  • Enterprise is for the conversation. No price shown. "Contact Sales" starts a relationship.

Pricing Evolution

These prices are C4/C5 launch prices. They will change:

  • C5 (furniture marketplace, XP, social): consider raising Growth to $3,500 (more features = more value)
  • C6 (white-label, enterprise, SDK): Enterprise tier becomes a formal product with structured pricing
  • C7 (multi-user): per-seat add-on pricing on top of base plan

The pricing config file makes changes instant. No code changes needed.

Launch Timing

This page should go live when C4's self-service signup is ready. Before that, the existing /system page with manual booking handles pricing conversations.

But the page should be BUILT during C3. Reasons:

  1. Bobby can build static pages in parallel with C3 game features
  2. Steffen designs the pricing page alongside C3 design specs
  3. Having the page ready means C4 self-service can launch immediately when containers work
  4. The page is also a sales tool: share the URL with prospects during outreach

The pricing page is the last thing a prospect sees before becoming a customer. It needs to be the most polished page on the site. Clean, confident, no surprises. "Your AI team. Pick your plan." That's it. Make it easy to say yes.
